To solve this question, I will recall the chemical behavior of acetylene when it reacts with strong bases.

Acetylene, which is a terminal alkyne, has acidic hydrogen atoms in its structure. When it reacts with a strong base, it tends to lose a hydrogen ion (H+) to form an acetylide ion. This is a well-known reaction and is commonly referred to as acetylide salt formation.
